name: kda_kv260_recurrence_bringup
causal_hypothesis: A banked on-chip KDA state store with parallel fixed-point lanes can execute the recurrent KDA head with deterministic latency and without sequence-length-dependent external state traffic.
stock_control: The bit-exact Python recurrence oracle. A real DDR-streamed FPGA control is deferred until the local-state core passes target-hardware correctness.
candidate: 128x128 state-local recurrence core with 16 parallel lanes and 16 block-RAM banks.

workload.state_format: signed 24-bit fixed point with 18 fractional bits

correctness_gate: Zero mismatches against the software oracle for all output elements across eight recurrent tokens, after an explicit state clear.
performance_outputs: DSP, LUT, flip-flop, and block-RAM use
slo: Close timing at 100 MHz and complete one 128x128 recurrence in 7168 core cycles or fewer.
cleanup: No external compute is allocated. Power down the KV260 after results are copied.
transfer_limits: This core measures one KDA recurrence head. It excludes Q/K/V projections, convolutional gate generation, normalization, residual addition, MoE, and full-model data movement.
The result cannot be compared directly with B300 or Vera Rubin token throughput.
Open-source synthesis is a resource proxy. Vivado implementation and KV260 execution are the next fidelity gates.
